title: AWS AI Practitioner & Generative AI
subtitle: Use AI, machine learning and generative AI services on AWS responsibly
audience_line: IT professionals, developers, analysts and managers working with AI on AWS
overview: This programme gives participants a practical understanding of AI, machine learning and generative AI on Amazon Web Services and prepares the AWS Certified AI Practitioner exam (AIF-C01). They learn the ML lifecycle and the ready-made AI services for vision, language, documents and speech, then the concepts behind foundation models, prompt engineering, and Amazon Bedrock with knowledge bases, agents and customisation. They use SageMaker Canvas and JumpStart, see what Amazon Q offers, and apply responsible AI, security and governance practices. Exam practice closes the content, and the programme ends with a final project: a generative AI assistant on Bedrock built and presented by each team.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: IT professionals, developers, analysts and managers working with AI on AWS

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: None in AI. Familiarity with core AWS services helps (course: AWS Cloud Practitioner) but is not required

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 33 h: 27 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs in the AWS console; exam practice

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant with a browser; one AWS sandbox account per team with Bedrock model access enabled and a budget alert, provided by the organiser; knowledge bases and endpoints deleted at the end of each lab to control cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase, practice exam questions and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete the labs and the project

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can choose the right AWS AI service for a use case, build a guarded RAG assistant with Bedrock, estimate its cost and sit the AIF-C01 exam

phases.name: AI & ML on AWS
phases.focus: AI and ML concepts, the ML lifecycle, ready-made AI services
phases.intro: Participants learn the vocabulary of AI and machine learning and the lifecycle of an ML project on AWS, then use ready-made services for images, text, documents, speech and translation without training a model. Validated lab: a document processed by Textract, its text analysed by Comprehend and its summary read aloud by Polly.

chapters.title: AI & ML Fundamentals
chapters.content: Concepts, the ML lifecycle on AWS

chapters.title: AWS AI Services
chapters.content: Rekognition, Comprehend, Textract, Lex, Polly, Transcribe, Translate

phases.name: Generative AI & Amazon Bedrock
phases.focus: Foundation models, prompting, Bedrock knowledge bases, agents and customisation
phases.intro: Participants learn how foundation models work and where they fail, write effective prompts, then build with Amazon Bedrock: model choice in the playgrounds, retrieval-augmented generation with Knowledge Bases, Agents and model customisation. Validated lab: a Bedrock Knowledge Base that answers questions over a set of company documents with cited sources.

chapters.title: Generative AI Concepts
chapters.content: Foundation models, tokens, embeddings, use cases and limits

chapters.title: Amazon Bedrock
chapters.content: Models, playgrounds, Knowledge Bases (RAG), Agents, customisation

phases.name: Tools, Responsible AI & Exam Preparation
phases.focus: SageMaker Canvas and JumpStart, Amazon Q, responsible AI, security, AIF-C01
phases.intro: Participants build a model without code in SageMaker Canvas and deploy a pretrained one from JumpStart, see the use cases of Amazon Q Business and Q Developer, apply responsible AI with Bedrock Guardrails and SageMaker Clarify, and secure and govern AI workloads before practising AIF-C01 questions. Validated lab: a Bedrock Guardrail that blocks a denied topic and masks personal data in the assistant's answers.

chapters.title: Amazon Q
chapters.content: Amazon Q Business and Q Developer use cases

chapters.title: Responsible AI
chapters.content: Bias, transparency, Bedrock Guardrails, SageMaker Clarify

chapters.title: Security & Governance
chapters.content: Data privacy, compliance for AI workloads

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A generative AI assistant on Bedrock, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three build an assistant for a company's documents from a written brief, reusing the phase labs, then present it with its cost estimate as they would to a business sponsor.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, build the Knowledge Base over the company documents, connect one AI service such as Textract

chapters.title: Guard & Estimate
chapters.content: Guardrails, test questions, cost estimate, architecture diagram

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo including a blocked request, cleanup; questions and feedback

project.title: A Generative AI Assistant on Bedrock
project.brief: An assistant that answers questions over company documents through a Bedrock Knowledge Base, reads scanned documents with an AI service such as Textract, is protected by Guardrails and comes with a cost estimate.
project.stack: AWS: Amazon Bedrock (Knowledge Bases, Guardrails), S3, Textract, AWS Pricing Calculator
project.deliverable: Working assistant, test questions and results, cost estimate, live demo
